name: Lighter Than It Should Be
summary: Somebody leaves carved toys on the five Krezkov graves at the Pool of the White Sun every night. Nobody in Krezk carves like that.

stages.journal: Krezk's watchman says there are carved toys on the Krezkov children's graves at the Pool of the White Sun every morning. Dmitri calls it mockery and smashes them. Anna keeps them.
objectives: Look at the Krezkov graves by the pool
stages.hint: Look at the Krezkov children's graves at the Pool of the White Sun in Krezk.

stages.journal: A wooden horse, a wolf, a little sun with too many rays: carved crude and sharp, as if with teeth. Most of them are on the eldest child's stone. Old Pavel, who carves suns for the shrine, swears they aren't his.
objectives: Watch the Krezkov graves after midnight
stages.hint: Watch the Krezkov graves at the Pool of the White Sun after midnight.

stages.journal: After midnight a hunched figure came over the north wall from the abbey road with a carved wolf in his hand: goat-legged, too big, with a boy's eyes. He knelt at the eldest Krezkov's stone and sang the lullaby Anna sings through her shutters, in Anna's own voice.
stages.hint: Talk to the figure at the Krezkov graves after midnight, gently.

stages.journal: He is Sorin Krezkov, Dmitri and Anna's first son. Twenty years ago Anna carried him up the mountain with the fever, against Dmitri's wishes, and the Abbot sent down a nailed coffin. It was lighter than it should have been. He has been improving Sorin ever since. Dmitri calls Ilya his last son.
objectives: Bring Sorin home to the Krezkovs
stages.hint: Bring Sorin to the Krezkovs' house in Krezk; the abbey may send someone after him.

stages.journal: The abbey came for its stray: Belview Brutes, and two brides the Abbot made before Vasilka, down the switchback with lanterns. We stopped them among the graves.
objectives: Bring Sorin home to the Krezkovs
stages.hint: Bring Sorin to the Krezkovs' house in Krezk.

stages.journal: Sorin Krezkov is home. Anna knew him before he'd finished his first word. Dmitri needed longer, and then he didn't need any time at all. Ilya has a brother who carves wolves.
Sorin stays at the Pool of the White Sun with Kasha Varo, who says she's needed a groundskeeper for forty years. Anna visits on Tuesdays, and on every other day too.
Sorin went back up the mountain. Dmitri couldn't look at him, and Sorin understood that better than we did. The toys still come, some mornings.
